Level 1 · Introduction · Week 11

Project Studio

Build, test and improve your project in small steps.

What you will learn

  • How real programmers build big programs: one small step at a time.
  • How to test a partner’s program and give helpful feedback.
  • How to finish Milestones M2 and M3 of your art show.

The big idea: build, run, check

Big programs are not written in one go. Programmers go round this loop all day long:

It is like building a LEGO set bag by bag: finish bag 1, check it looks like the picture, then open bag 2.

Your milestones

Five small steps (the tiny art show from the demo)

  1. Question: how_many = int(input("How many bubbles? ")). Run.

  2. Function: def bubble(x, y, color): and call it once. Run.

  3. Loop: put the call inside for i in range(how_many):. Run.

  4. Random: random x, y and color. Run twice!

  5. If: if the number is too big, use a smaller one. Run with 500.

TipSave a version

Before a big change, click File → Save as… and add _v2 to the name (fish_party_v2.py). If the change goes wrong, version 1 is still safe.

Exercise11.1: Sprint 1: core drawing works (M2)

Open your project file. Change the example my_shape function into your function: give it a name that says what it draws, and change the drawing. Draw it once at (0, 0). Run. Then call it a second time somewhere else. Run.

Exercise11.2: Partner bug hunt

Swap seats with your partner. Run their program twice: once with a normal answer, once with a strange one (0, a giant number, a word, a capital letter). Write what happened — don’t fix it, just report it!

I typed What happened

Then give two stars and a wish:

★ I liked (blank to fill in)

★ I liked (blank to fill in)

 I wish (blank to fill in)

Exercise11.3: Sprint 2: surprise and polish (M3)

Add the rest of your six ingredients. Check off each one in the comment list at the top of your file when you have seen it work.

TipFeedback is a gift

Giving: be kind and specific (“I like how the stars are different sizes”), and make wishes about the program, never the person. Getting: say thank you — then you decide what to change. It is your art.

Reflect

What bug did you find today? How did you find it?

What feedback did you get? What will you change because of it?

New words

Iterate
To improve something by going round the build–run–check loop again and again.
Milestone
A checkpoint on the way to finishing a project.
Playtest
Letting someone else try your program to find problems.
Feedback
What someone tells you about your work, to help you improve it.
Version
A saved copy of your program at one moment, like _v2 .

Homework: Get Ready for the Showcase

15–20 minutes. This week's homework is project work: finish and practice.

CoreFinish and practice (about 10 minutes)

  1. If your project is missing an ingredient, add it now (or write on paper how you will add it next week). Which ingredients still need work?

  2. Practice your 2-minute demo out loud for someone at home. They are the visitor: let them answer your program’s question (or pretend, using your sketch). Use the script in your workbook (chapter 12).

  3. Ask your visitor for two stars and a wish:

    ★ (blank to fill in)

    ★ (blank to fill in)

     (blank to fill in)

ChallengeBe ready for strange answers

Visitors sometimes type surprising things. Make your program cope:

  • a number that is too big? Use an if to make it smaller and print a friendly message;

  • Night instead of night? Add .lower() after input(...).

CreativeMake your stand card

Fold a piece of paper in half to make a card that stands up. Write your project’s title, your nickname as the artist, and one sentence about your artwork. Decorate it! (No real full names, please: nicknames only.)

Self-checkSelf-check: tick each box when it is true
